summary: The Quest for El Dorado is a deck-building race game where players build a deck of movement cards to traverse a modular jungle path as fast as possible. It's approachable and quick, blending deck-building strategy with a straightforward race to the finish.
praised: Very approachable entry point into deck-building for newer gamers
Good variable routes and modular board keep it fresh
criticised: Less strategic depth than heavier deck-builders
Can feel like a solitaire race with limited direct interaction
Card draw luck affects a given turn's options
Some find repeated plays get a bit samey

interaction.kind: racing and blocking on a shared path
interaction.detail: All players move their pieces along the same modular board toward the goal, and since a space can only hold one piece, players routinely block each other's routes and force detours. Expedition cards are also bought from a shared visible market, so grabbing one can deny it to a rival, though no card lets a player act directly on an opponent's team.

sources: spaces advanced via played movement/action cards
scoring.how_you_win: Build a deck of movement and helper cards to cross the board fastest; the first player to reach the golden temple wins outright, no scoring needed.
scoring.score_note: pure race to the border, no score
